<p class="eyebrow">R package · Public release v0.3.4 · Submitted to CRAN; review pending</p>

**Authors:** Silas Bambil and Yasmeen Babagana.

**bambaganaCI** provides confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, descriptive summaries, association measures, linear-model inference, analysis of variance, and model-based power planning. The package has **40 statistical functions** and **43 public exports**. The public release provides a beginner-friendly `bambagana()` interface for selecting analyses by readable names; the original statistical functions remain directly accessible.

Version 0.3.4 is the [latest public GitHub release](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI/releases/tag/v0.3.4). A later, separately validated v0.3.4 source archive was submitted to CRAN on November 14, 2026, and the submission has been confirmed. **CRAN review is pending. The package is not yet available on CRAN.**

## Install from GitHub

Install from the formal v0.3.4 release tag to obtain the documented version.

```{.r}
install.packages("remotes") # Only if remotes is not installed
remotes::install_github(
  "sdbambil1/bambaganaCI",
  ref = "v0.3.4"
)
library(bambaganaCI)
packageVersion("bambaganaCI")
```

[View source](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI) · [v0.3.4 release](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI/releases/tag/v0.3.4) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI/issues)

## Start with readable commands

```{.r}
library(bambaganaCI)

scores <- c(65, 72, 68, 75, 70, 78, 74, 69, 73, 76)
group_B <- c(71, 79, 75, 82, 77, 85, 80, 74, 78, 81)

bambagana("descriptive statistics", scores)
bambagana("confidence interval", scores)
bambagana("confidence interval", scores, conf = 0.99)
bambagana("standard error", scores)
bambagana("compare averages", scores, group_B)
bambagana("hypothesis test", scores, mu = 70)
bambagana("compare proportions", c(65, 100), c(45, 100))

# Browse all 40 statistical functions and their arguments
bambagana("all functions")
```

The general confidence-interval command above estimates a **population mean**. Proportions, differences between groups, and other quantities have their own analysis commands. Statistical results are preserved: use `display = FALSE` to save a result without automatic console printing.

## Supported confidence intervals

The original package provides percentile, basic, normal, and bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstrap intervals for a population mean, as well as a classical Student's t interval.

| Method | Function or option | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Percentile bootstrap | `method = "percentile"` | Uses quantiles of resampled means |
| Basic bootstrap | `method = "basic"` | Reflects bootstrap quantiles about the sample mean |
| Normal bootstrap | `method = "normal"` | Uses bootstrap standard error and bias adjustment |
| BCa bootstrap | `method = "bca"` | Adjusts endpoints for bias and acceleration |
| Student's t interval | `mean_t_ci()` | Uses the t distribution and sample standard error |

```{.r}
set.seed(1998)
x <- rnorm(30, mean = 2, sd = 1)

result <- bambagana(
  "bootstrap confidence interval",
  x, B = 2000, method = "percentile",
  display = FALSE
)
print(result)

comparison <- compare_mean_ci(
  x, B = 2000, conf = 0.95,
  methods = c("percentile", "basic", "normal", "bca", "t")
)
print(comparison)
```

## Linear regression and ANOVA

The simplified interface returns the original fitted model objects. Standard R methods can therefore be used for coefficient intervals and prediction.

```{.r}
employees <- data.frame(
  experience = 1:10,
  salary = c(32, 35, 37, 41, 43, 46, 50, 51, 55, 59)
)

model <- bambagana(
  "linear regression",
  salary ~ experience,
  data = employees,
  display = FALSE
)

coef(model)
confint(model)
predict(model, newdata = data.frame(experience = 5))
```

For analysis of variance, use `bambagana("anova", scores, group)`, with a grouping factor of the same length as the score vector.

## Package verification

The public GitHub v0.3.4 release and the subsequent CRAN submission archive are distinct builds. The final submission archive includes documentation and maintainer-contact updates made after the GitHub release. Earlier v0.3.4 builds were checked across three environments:

| Environment | Result | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| macOS, R 4.4.1 | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 NOTES | New submission; current time could not be verified |
| Windows R-devel, Winbuilder | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 NOTE | The email report gives the overall status; the NOTE detail has not been independently inspected |
| Linux, Ubuntu 26.04.1, R 4.6.2 | 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 NOTE | New submission; tests, examples, documentation, and vignettes passed |

The **final CRAN submission archive** was built with R 4.6.2 and checked using `R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual` on Linux. The result was **0 errors, 0 warnings, and 1 NOTE (`New submission`)**. The [final validation report](https://github.com/sdbambil1/bambaganaCI/actions/runs/43553612328) documents this check. The Windows R-release result and PDF manual generation have not been independently verified for the final archive. The CRAN submission was confirmed on November 14, 2026; **acceptance and publication remain pending**. Package checks do not demonstrate nominal interval coverage for every data-generating process.

## Assumptions and limitations

The appropriate assumptions depend on the chosen method. Ordinary bootstrap intervals for a mean generally assume independent, identically distributed observations. The classical t interval has exact coverage under independent normal sampling with positive common variance. Some tests and intervals rely on approximations, which may be less reliable for small, highly skewed, heavy-tailed, or sparse samples. The package does not automatically correct for clustered data, serial dependence, complex survey designs, or unhandled missing observations. Users should review method-specific documentation before drawing inferential conclusions.
